hens_rule_text: 1 chicken per 1,000 sq ft of lot area, up to a maximum of 10 chickens on any single lot, allowed as a limited 'restricted agriculture' accessory use distinct from the full Agriculture use category (which is not allowed in Residential Districts).
permit_notes: No permit specific to chickens was found; the coop itself is treated as an accessory structure subject to standard zoning permitting for structures.
setback_notes: Coops, hutches and similar structures must be at least 25 ft from any property line (not specifically from a neighbor's dwelling), per UDO Sec. 6.6.1, and must also meet the accessory structure setback rules of Sec. 6.6.1/6.6 generally; the coop cannot be in the front yard.
coop_rules: Coop, hutch or similar animal housing structure must sit at least 25 ft from any property line and cannot be located in the front yard.
zoning_notes: Raleigh's UDO Sec. 6.6.1 treats broad 'Agriculture' as not permitted in Residential Districts, but a narrower 'restricted agriculture' category allows a small number of chickens (the 1 per 1,000 sq ft/10 max rule) as an accessory residential use; this distinction is drawn from secondary summaries and could not be confirmed by reading the Restricted Agriculture subsection directly.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: coopcraftguide.com, Raleigh North Carolina Chicken Laws

research_notes: Read the top-level Sec. 6.6.1 Agriculture page directly on udo.raleighnc.gov, which lists 'Restricted agriculture' as a separate use from full Agriculture (the latter not permitted in Residential Districts), but the page's Restricted Agriculture subsection with the specific chicken numbers did not load in full; the 1-per-1,000-sq-ft/10-max/no-rooster/25-ft rule is corroborated by multiple secondary chicken-law summaries that cite the same UDO section.
